evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.reading: Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken (melee wielder) / +5% (ranged wielder), applying to damage FROM ALL SOURCES, i.e. a debuff on the target that amplifies the whole allied roster's damage, not only the Bloodsong holder's.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> {{rd|melee|ranged}} template convention, cross-checked across the cache
sources_quoted.quote: Ravenous Hydra {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Titanic Hydra {{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}%}}; Death's Dance {{rd|30%|10%}}; Eclipse {{rd|6%|4%}}; Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}}
sources_quoted.reading: First argument is the melee value, second the reduced ranged value (every cross-checked item follows melee-first). Therefore Bloodsong Expose Weakness is 8% for a melee wielder, 5% for a ranged wielder.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.reading: Carve is likewise a target debuff (armor reduction), so its benefit is team-wide; C = 5 stacks, 6% each, hard cap 30%.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 item 2 (Black Cleaver average stacks)
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed `0.8·max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesàro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C − C(C−1)/(2h)` for `h ≥ C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to ±20% at the extremes... **Recommendation:** replace the constant with the closed-form Cesàro mean
sources_quoted.reading: The pre-change BC model is an explicitly documented APPROXIMATION that UNDERSTATES shred for fights longer than ~10 hits; the exact model is 5 − 10/h stacks, ceiling 5 stacks / 30%.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.1 and the Section 5 audit table
sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)   (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... raw = post · (1 + R/100)
sources_quoted.reading: Mitigation is linear in raw damage for fixed R, so a uniform target-debuff amp or a uniform shred change scales the team damage total multiplicatively — which is what makes the ratio test below valid.
Used only for the secondary decomposition D3 below (level-18 growth multiplier is exactly 17: 17·(0.7025 + 0.0175·17) = 17·1.0).

independent_computation.limitation_stated_up_front: The scenario's participant roster, levels, item loadouts, ranks and fight window live in scripts/ and tests/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from reading. The absolute 4-digit total therefore cannot be re-derived from first principles inside the permitted evidence tree. What CAN be computed independently from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md is (a) the wiki-sourced constants that govern this scenario, and (b) a ratio/envelope test on the moved leaf, which is decisive on direction.

step_1_ratio.note: +2.7534% — a small, uniform multiplicative lift, the signature of a target-debuff term (amp or shred) rather than a new damage instance on one participant.

expose_weakness_ranged_to_melee_ceiling.test: observed 1.0275344 ≤ 1.0285714 — ADMISSIBLE, and sits at 96.4% of the ceiling

black_cleaver_constant_to_exact_mean_cei.test: observed 1.0275344 is ADMISSIBLE only for A ≳ 70; it exceeds the A=50 ceiling. Implied exact-mean stacks would be 4.79 (A=100), 4.64 (A=150), 4.56 (A=200) — i.e. h ≈ 47, 28, 23 stacking hits via h = 10/(5 − stacks). All below the 5-stack / 30% cap.

step_2_wiki_ceilings.conclusion: Under EVERY wiki-admissible reading, the NEW value lies inside the wiki-sourced envelope and the OLD value lies strictly below it. No reading was found in which the new value exceeds a wiki ceiling (it exceeds neither the 8%/5% amp ratio nor the 30% Carve cap).

step_3_exact_decompositions.note: Each decomposition solves old = U + a_old·X, new = U + a_new·X for the amped sub-total X and the un-amped remainder U. All are self-consistent (U, X ≥ 0).

D1_expose_weakness_5pct_to_8pct.plausibility: STRONG. 3.8% of the fight's damage landing before the first Expose Weakness application matches the wiki's own timing clause — 'starts after using the empowered attack' — i.e. only the pre-first-spellblade damage escapes the debuff, and the 4 s duration vs 1.5 s cooldown gives ~100% uptime thereafter.

D2_expose_weakness_extended_to_all_sourc.plausibility: STRONG. If the pre-change model amped only the Bloodsong holder's damage, extending it to the rest of the roster (which the wiki text 'from all sources' requires) lifts the team total by 8% of the allies' 34.4% share. A 'roster' scenario is exactly the fixture that would expose this.

D3_one_missing_spellblade_proc.plausibility: WEAK/COINCIDENTAL. Offered only for completeness — the scenario roster is not readable from the permitted tree, so the champion identity is unverified. Direction is the same: a wiki-sourced term ('deals 100% base AD bonus physical damage on-hit') being priced where it previously was not.

D4_black_cleaver_constant_to_cesaro_mean.plausibility: MODERATE. docs/math-foundations.md §2.3 names this exact replacement as the recommended fix and warns it 're-tunes every BC fight in the corpus'. It also fixes the sign: the constant UNDERSTATES shred for h > 10, so replacing it can only raise damage — which is the observed direction.

step_4_falsification_attempt.question: Is there any wiki-admissible model under which 4074.9 is exact and 4187.1 over-applies?
checks: Double-application of Expose Weakness would need ratio > 1.08 (or 1.08·1.08/1.05 = 1.110 over the 5% base); observed 1.0275 is far below — REJECTED.

Carve stacking past its cap would need ratio > the A-dependent 30%-cap ceiling; observed 1.0275 is below every such ceiling for A ≳ 70 and BC alone cannot even reach it for A ≲ 50 — REJECTED as an over-application.

Applying the melee 8% to a ranged Bloodsong wielder is the only construction that would make the old value the correct one. It cannot be excluded from the permitted tree (the wielder's attackType is scenario data), but it is the least likely: the cache's own template convention makes 8% the primary value, Bloodsong is paired here with Black Cleaver (a 400 HP / 40 AD / 20 AH melee-bruiser line), and no other decomposition requires a ranged wielder.
step_4_falsification_attempt.result: No admissible over-application found. Every construction that fits the magnitude and sign has the old value UNDER-applying a term the cached wiki text authorises (the 8% melee Expose Weakness value, the 'from all sources' team-wide scope, the 100% base AD spellblade instance, or the exact Carve stack mean in place of the documented 0.8·max_stacks approximation).

independent_computation.confidence: High on direction and envelope; the absolute total is not independently reproducible without scripts/ and tests/, which this runbook forbids. Stated explicitly rather than papered over.

verdict_rationale: The moved leaf is a team-damage total in a scenario whose two named items — Black Cleaver's Carve and Bloodsong's Expose Weakness — are both TARGET debuffs, so both amplify the whole roster's damage per the cached wiki text. The +2.7534% lift sits inside every wiki-sourced ceiling (1.08/1.05 = 1.0285714 for the melee/ranged amp; the 30%-cap ceiling for Carve) and strictly closer to the exact model than the old value, and it admits clean self-consistent decompositions (X = 3740.0 amped / U = 147.9 un-amped for a 5%→8% correction; 1402.5 newly-amped ally damage for a holder-only → all-sources correction). docs/math-foundations.md §2.3 independently establishes that the pre-change Black Cleaver constant UNDERSTATES shred for fights past ~10 hits and recommends the exact Cesàro mean, which also predicts an increase. No wiki-admissible construction makes the new value an over-application. Verdict: new_value_correct.
